items.title: Nanbeige4.3-33B: open-weight 33B dense agentic coding model (512K context) posts Terminal-Bench 2.1 80.9 vs Qwen3.8-27B 73.0
items.summary: Nanbeige (Kanzhun's lab) released Nanbeige4.3-33B and a Base checkpoint on Hugging Face: a 33B dense BF16 model with 512K context aimed at coding and cowork agents. The model card reports Terminal-Bench 2.1 80.9 vs 73.0 for Qwen3.8-27B, DeepSWE 65.5 vs 42.5, and SWE-Bench Pro 60.3 vs 61.7 (slightly behind), with serving examples for Transformers, SGLang and vLLM. The lab says the model is the teacher for an upcoming Nanbeige4.3-3B. Benchmarks are self-reported.

doubt.pushback: @teortaxesTex calls the results plausible but fragile and at risk of doom looping; several repliers ask whether it is benchmaxxed and whether eval tasks were kept out of training data.

reception.summary: Quotes and replies are mostly excitement and 'downloading now'; nobody had posted hands-on results yet. Open questions are benchmaxxing, tool-call latency, official GGUF/FP8 builds, and fitting a 33B dense model with long KV cache on 24 to 32 GB cards.

items.title: llama.cpp b11870 adds DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash support
items.summary: llama.cpp pre-release b11870 (published 2026-10-25 02:15 UTC on GitHub) adds the deepseek41 architecture so DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash can run locally through GGUF; the change is co-authored by Daniel Han and includes a Metal fusion test. Verified on the GitHub release page; the X post itself has low engagement.

items.title: Sebastian Raschka posts full Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch) video course: 8 videos, 11 hours of PyTorch code
items.summary: Raschka published all eight coding lectures for Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch): starting from a pre-trained Qwen3 0.6B, the course implements KV caching, a MATH-500 verifier, self-consistency and self-refinement, a simplified GRPO for RLVR with clipping and KL terms, and distillation from DeepSeek R1 outputs, all in Python and PyTorch with per-chapter code in the companion repo.

doubt.source: Course page with all eight videos and chapter code links.

reception.summary: Repliers welcome having the whole series in one place and ask which chapter to start with, whether it covers material beyond the book, and whether RL on tool calling is coming next.

security_forwarded.matched: Hermes agent, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor CLI; always_forward: agent tooling
security_forwarded.note: GitSpawn (Manifold, disclosed 2026-09-02): a repo delivered as files with .git intact (zip, synced folder, shared drive; not a normal clone) can set core.fsmonitor so the agent's background git status runs attacker code outside the sandbox and before any prompt. Fixed: Claude Code 2.1.196 (core.fsmonitor path; a separate 'ultrareview' path was still live on 2.1.252 per CSA), Codex CLI 0.131.0 (CVE-2026-19592) and Desktop 26.519.x, Cursor, Goose 1.44.0. Hermes Agent 0.18.2 to 0.21.0 is CVE-2026-71963 (CVSS 8.6), fixed only in commit f6234d0 / 0.21.1+, so a 0.21.0 tag is still vulnerable. Verified: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-71963 , https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/malicious-git-configs-can-make-claude.html , https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-gitspawn-ai-coding-agent-rce-20260903-csa/ . Box: no claude, codex, hermes, cursor-agent or goose binaries; no global core.fsmonitor. Suggested check: agent versions on Mac/Mini/Air/Spark and git config --global core.fsmonitor false.
